themes.label: Stand-down tripped at Tuesday's close; NVDA relief pre-market
themes.narrative: The market is reading NVDA's report as a relief: the headline flow is 'equities set to rebound as investors parse Nvidia results', and NVDA is bid pre-market.
themes.dataAnchor: Tuesday's close tripped both lines: VIX closed at 25.46 (+11.13%, its 5-day high, no rollover) and SPX closed at 7,340.53, 0.05% below its 200-day $7,344.53 and 6.42% below its 120-day high. Pre-market Wednesday: VIX 24.66, back under 25; SPY $733.75 vs Tuesday's $732.44 close; NVDA $159.60 vs its $155.46 close (+2.7%).
themes.counterRead: A pre-market bid is not a close. The stand-down governs until VIX closes back under 25, and today's close is the second-close test for SPX below its 200-day. The earnings details themselves are not in this input, so the read is the price reaction only — and a relief gap on an oversold stock is exactly the trap setup.
themes.watchFor: Today's close: VIX under 25 lifts the stand-down; SPX below $7,344.53 for a second close confirms the escalation rung.

themes.label: AI infrastructure: fundamentals ahead of price, print now out
themes.narrative: The market has priced the AI build-out as peaked: NVDA is down 28.4% over the month and 36.1% below its 52-week high, and SMH closed Tuesday 31.52% below its 120-day high.
themes.dataAnchor: Revenue keeps growing while prices fall: AVGO +55% YoY at 31% below its high (score 81, tier A, reports Dec 9); DDOG +27.7% YoY, 80% gross margin, $1,001M FCF, 45.1% below its high (score 84, tier A); ONTO 48.4% below (score 81); AMAT 52.8% below (score 80). NVDA was promoted to the conviction tier (score 83, revenue +61.4% YoY) and closed Tuesday at $155.46 with RSI 22.5; SMH $460.10 is 12.27% below its 200-day; both remain below Zone 2.
themes.counterRead: The print was the catalyst this theme was waiting on, and the first reaction is positive pre-market. But re-arming needs closes, not quotes: NVDA must close back above its $175 Zone 2 floor (12.6% above Tuesday's close) and SMH back inside $470-505. A one-day relief that fades leaves these names DATA_AHEAD but not actionable.
themes.watchFor: NVDA close vs $175 and SMH close vs $470 over the next two sessions.

themes.label: Rotation, not rollover — index now giving ground
themes.narrative: Credit still reads the selloff as leadership rotation, not a broad rollover, even as the index slips under its 200-day.
themes.dataAnchor: Mag7 averages 19.16% below 52-week highs versus SPY at 6.3%, a 12.86-point divergence gap; weakest NVDA at 36.1% below, strongest AAPL at 2.5%. Lending standards LOOSE (SLOOS 1.7%); HY OAS 3.34. SPY is down 3.78% over the month and 5.04% over three months; IWM down 11.84% over three months.
themes.counterRead: The rotation read survives on credit alone — the mechanical tally is 1 of 4, and the one confirmed signal is credit calm. SPY is about 38% of the portfolio; if HY OAS starts widening toward 4%, the rotation read and the portfolio's ballast fail together.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS move above 4%, or the Mag7/SPY divergence gap past 20 points.

themes.label: Nuclear / AI power still bleeding
themes.narrative: The nuclear and AI-power names trade as an AI-capex derivative and keep getting sold with the semis.
themes.dataAnchor: VST closed Tuesday at $127.15, 32.8% below its peak, down 15.1% over the month, RSI 42.1; insiders bought $1.17M at the trough, but its score fell to 75 (watchlist, down from the conviction tier) and its decline reason now reads ACUTE_CATALYST rather than sentiment. VRT closed at $190.37, 49.9% below its peak. Over the month: SMR -27.42%, CCJ -19.6%, OKLO -17.14%, URA -14.66%.
themes.counterRead: VST and VRT are holdings, so this is a hold decision. If NVDA's relief holds, the power names are next in line for a bounce; if it fades, they lack their own catalyst — VST's revenue reads STABLE_OR_DECLINING and the screen now flags an acute catalyst behind the decline, so the insider-buying argument is weaker than last week.
themes.watchFor: VST, CCJ and SMR: two consecutive closes without new lows.

themes.label: Leveraged and crypto complex still unwinding
themes.narrative: The leveraged and crypto complex is being sold as one risk bucket, and crypto is not confirming any rebound.
themes.dataAnchor: Over the month: CONL -55.69%, TQQQ -25.31%, BMNR -25.59%, DOGE -25.63%, COIN -31.17%, IBIT -21.9%, ETH-USD -23.88%, BTC-USD -21.28%. CONL closed Tuesday at $2.00; TQQQ at $51.81.
themes.counterRead: TQQQ, CONL, BMNR and DOGE are holdings and carry the most leverage to whatever NVDA's relief becomes. The no-averaging-down rule applies until the stand-down lifts; a relief day in TQQQ is not a reason to add.
themes.watchFor: BTC: a fresh -5% day re-opens the unwind; two up days while equities hold would be the first confirmation of a pause.

strategyPosture: Watch, with the stand-down in force: VIX closed above 25 and SPX closed below its 200-day on Tuesday. No new money and no averaging down until VIX closes back under 25; the pre-market NVDA bid does not change that before the close.
whereWaveBuilds: Today's close decides whether NVDA's report turns into a relief leg: VIX closing under 25 with SPX back above $7,344.53 lifts the stand-down and opens a move toward the SPX failure zone $7,750-7,820, while a second close below the 200-day confirms the next leg down. FOMC minutes at 2 pm ET are the second trigger today.
watchFor: VIX close: under 25 lifts the stand-down; above 25 keeps it.
SPX close vs its 200-day $7,344.53 — a second close below confirms the escalation rung.
NVDA close vs its $175 Zone 2 floor; SMH close vs its $470 floor.
FOMC minutes at 2 pm ET: a hawkish read with the 10Y above 5.12% pressures long-duration growth.
HY OAS above 4% trips the stand-down regardless of equities.

reaction.episode: CORRECTION episode through the Nov 17 close: SPX 7,340.53, 6.42% below its 120-day high and 0.05% below its 200-day $7,344.53; SMH $460.10 and NVDA $155.46 both below Zone 2; VIX 25.46 at its 5-day high with no rollover; HY OAS 3.34; tally 1 of 4. Both stand-down lines tripped at Tuesday's close. Pre-market Nov 18: VIX 24.66, NVDA $159.60 after its report.

ladder.trigger: SPX closes below its 200-day $7,344.53 for a second session
ladder.response: Hold cash, no buys; wait for a failed first bounce and a second low that holds before re-checking bottom conditions.

ladder.trigger: VIX closes above 25 or HY OAS above 4% (VIX tripped Nov 17)
ladder.response: Stand down all deployment until both are back below their lines; no averaging down in TQQQ, CONL or BMNR.

ladder.trigger: NVDA's relief carries SPX into the failure zone $7,750-7,820, or SMH into $580-600
ladder.response: Treat as the bull-trap test: no chasing. Require a close above the zone plus a tally of at least 3 before any Add.

ladder.trigger: NVDA closes back above $175 AND SMH closes inside Zone 2 $470-505 AND tally at least 3 of 4
ladder.response: Re-entry review: move AVGO, DDOG and ONTO to Probe; size only on a second confirming close.

reaction.invalidation: An SPX close above $7,820 with SMH above $600 and the tally at least 3 voids the Watch stance and flips the posture to Probe/Add; HY OAS above 4% voids the 'correction, not crisis' read and the ladder with it.
reaction.trapRisk: This morning is the trap setup the ladder was written for: NVDA closed oversold (RSI 22.5) and is gapping up on the print. Entries do not happen on the gap-up open or while the stand-down is in force; they wait for VIX to close under 25, the failure-zone retest verdict, and a second low that holds.
